dicas.texto: Para transformar qualquer número em 100, qual operação matemática podemos usar para encontrar a proporção?
Tente dividir o número original (175) pelo número que você deseja obter (100). O resultado dessa divisão é o seu fator de escala.
Você está quase lá! Divida 175 por 100. O valor que encontrar será o fator que você deve usar para dividir tanto o numerador quanto o denominador.
O fator de escala é 175 dividido por 100. Calcule 175 / 100 e use esse valor para realizar a divisão em ambos os termos da razão.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: For each ratio, place the part being considered above the total collection.
Use the number of bands in the selected group as the numerator and the total number of bands as the denominator.
The total collection is used as the denominator in all three rows.
Fill the three rows in order: the whole collection over the whole collection, the blue bands over the collection, and the combined bands over the collection.
The scale factor must transform the original denominator into the target denominator of 100.
Find the factor by dividing the original denominator by the target denominator, then use the same factor on the numerator.
Because 175 must become the smaller number 100, choose division rather than multiplication.
Select division in both operation controls and enter the same factor, 1.75, in both scale-factor fields.
The numerator and denominator must be changed by the same factor so the ratio keeps its meaning.
Apply the selected division operation to the Part 1 numerator by dividing 84 by 1.75.
Think about how many groups of 1.75 fit into 84, then use that number as the numerator over 100.
Complete the final division of 84 by 1.75, then enter that result in both the percentage numerator field and the percentage field.
The target denominator is still 100, so compare the Part 2 denominator with 100.
Use the same scale-factor process: transform 175 into 100 and apply that transformation to both terms.
The original denominator is larger than 100, so select division and use the factor associated with 175 becoming 100.
Choose division for both controls and enter the same scale factor in the numerator and denominator fields.
The combined group is another part of the same total collection, so it must use the same ratio transformation.
Use the Part 2 operation and divide its numerator by the chosen scale factor.
Start with 126 and divide by 1.75 to obtain the numerator over 100.
Carry out the final division of 126 by 1.75, then enter the result in both Part 2 percentage fields.
The entire collection represents the whole, so its percentage must represent all of the collection.
Transform the total ratio in the same way as the other rows, then record the equivalent numerator over 100.
Use division by 1.75 for both total terms, and enter the resulting total numerator in the percentage fields.
Finish the Total row, confirm that the scale-factor fields use 1.75, and then activate Done to submit the completed table.

exercicio.statement:
David loves to collect Funny Bands. He currently has 175 bands in his collection. He is trying to figure out what percentage of each kind he has.

Part 1) Since blue is his favorite color, he has traded bands to obtain 84 blue bands. What percentage of his collection is now blue?

Part 2) He already had 42 animal skin bands. His 126 blue and animal skin bands make up what percentage of his collection? Part 1) Since blue is his favorite color, he has traded bands to obtain 84 blue bands. What percentage of his collection is now blue?
Part 2) He already had 42 animal skin bands. His 126 blue and animal skin bands make up what percentage of his collection?

hints.message: The entire collection represents the whole, so its percentage must represent all of the collection.
Transform the total ratio in the same way as the other rows, then record the equivalent numerator over 100.
Use division by 1.75 for both total terms, and enter the resulting total numerator in the percentage fields.
Finish the Total row, confirm that the scale-factor fields use 1.75, and then activate Done to submit the completed table.
